text: He made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide—square—and three cubits high.
He made horns for it on its four corners, the horns being of one piece with it, and he overlaid it with bronze.
He made all the utensils of the altar: the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the fire pans. All its utensils he made of bronze.
For the altar he made a grating of bronze network, under its ledge, reaching halfway up.
He cast four rings at the four corners of the bronze grating as holders for the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
He inserted the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar, so that it could be carried with them. He made it hollow, out of boards.

versions.text: He inserted the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar, so that it could be carried with them. He made it hollow, of boards.
versions.explanation: "of boards" standing alone after a comma reads abruptly; "out of boards" completes the clause more naturally when spoken.

text: He made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Then he made the courtyard. On the south side the hangings of the courtyard were of finely twisted linen, a hundred cubits long,
with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
On the north side the hangings were a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
On the west side the hangings were fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases; the hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
On the east side, toward the sunrise, the courtyard was fifty cubits wide.
The hangings on one side of the entrance were fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,
and on the other side of the courtyard gate—on this side and on that—the hangings were fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
All the hangings around the courtyard were of finely twisted linen.
The bases for the posts were bronze, the hooks of the posts and their bands were silver, and the tops of the posts were overlaid with silver; all the posts of the courtyard were banded with silver.

The screen for the gate of the courtyard was the work of an embroiderer, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen. It was twenty cubits long and, like the hangings of the courtyard, five cubits high,
with four posts and four bronze bases. Their hooks were silver, the overlay of their tops was silver, and their bands were silver.

versions.text: with four posts and four bronze bases. Their hooks were silver, and the tops of the posts and their bands were overlaid with silver.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says the overlay of the capitals was silver and the bands were silver; the current wording implies the bands themselves were "overlaid with silver," which the text does not say (compare verses 10-12 and 17, where the bands are simply silver).

text: All the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the surrounding courtyard were of bronze.
These are the records of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, drawn up at Moses' command by the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything the LORD had commanded Moses,
and with him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, a craftsman and designer, and an embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
All the gold used for the work, for every part of the sanctuary work—the gold of the wave offering—came to twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.

versions.text: All the gold used for the work, in all the work of the sanctuary—the gold from the wave offering—came to twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
versions.explanation: The repetition of "the work, in all the work" is clumsy for oral reading; "for every part of the sanctuary work" keeps the sense of בְּכֹל מְלֶאכֶת הַקֹּדֶשׁ while flowing better.

text: The silver from those of the congregation who were counted came to a hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels, by the sanctuary shekel:
one beka per person, that is, half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel, from everyone registered in the census, twenty years old and upward—six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty men.

versions.text: one beka per person, that is, half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel, from everyone who crossed over to those counted, twenty years old and upward—six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty men.
versions.explanation: "crossed over to those counted" is a literal rendering that sounds opaque and stumbles when read aloud. "Everyone registered in the census" conveys the same idiom (passing over among those numbered) clearly and rhythmically.

text: The hundred talents of silver were used to cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the curtain—a hundred bases from the hundred talents, one talent per base.
From the one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels he made hooks for the posts, overlaid their tops, and made bands for them.
The bronze from the wave offering came to seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar with its bronze grating, and all the utensils of the altar,
the bases around the courtyard and the bases of the courtyard gate, and all the tent pegs of the tabernacle and all the tent pegs around the courtyard.
